keyVerseText: And he said, I will make all my goodness pass before thee, and I will proclaim the name of the LORD before thee; and will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will shew mercy on whom I will shew mercy.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew verb רָחַם (râcham) is a primitive root that fundamentally conveys a deep, tender affection, often expressed as compassion or mercy. Its core sense involves a visceral, almost physical tenderness akin to fondling, which by extension implies a profound, compassionate love. This root meaning enriches the common English glosses like 'have compassion' or 'show mercy' by emphasizing not just an abstract feeling but an intimate, heartfelt affection.
usageInScripture: The word רָחַם occurs 47 times in the Hebrew Bible, consistently conveying God's compassionate and merciful disposition toward His people. It is translated variously as 'have mercy,' 'have compassion,' and 'will shew mercy,' reflecting a consistent theological theme of tender, active love. The range of translations, though nuanced, centers on God's gracious and affectionate response, underscoring both His willingness and sovereign choice in showing mercy.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding רָחַם as an expression of tender, compassionate love is vital for grasping the nature of God's relationship with His people. It reveals a God who is not distant or indifferent but deeply moved by the plight of His creation, choosing to exercise mercy according to His sovereign will. This word highlights the personal and relational character of divine mercy, which is foundational to the gospel message of redemption and grace. For believers, it assures that God's compassion is both intentional and affectionate, inviting trust and worship.
keyVerseReflection: In Exodus 33:19, God declares that He will be 'gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will shew mercy on whom I will shew mercy.' The use of רָחַם here underscores God's sovereign and gracious choice to extend tender compassion and mercy. This verse powerfully reveals that God's mercy is not arbitrary but a deliberate expression of His goodness, inviting us to marvel at His gracious character and to rest in His loving kindness.
